items.title: 13.9 Reactions of halides (X-) with concentrated sulfuric acid

blocks.text: The halide ions react differently with concentrated sulfuric acid; the products and the nature of the reaction change down the group. With sodium fluoride, fumes of hydrogen fluoride are produced, NaF(s) + H2SO4(l) gives NaHSO4 + HF(g); HF is a weak reducing agent and does not react further. With sodium chloride, fumes of hydrogen chloride: NaCl(s) + H2SO4(l) gives NaHSO4 + HCl(g). With bromide, steamy fumes of hydrogen bromide and brown fumes of bromine are produced with the smell of sulfur dioxide, a redox reaction in which HBr reduces sulfuric acid to SO2 and is itself oxidised to bromine: NaBr + H2SO4 gives NaHSO4 + HBr, then 2HBr(s) + H2SO4 gives Br2 + 2SO2 + 2H2O. With sodium iodide, fumes of hydrogen iodide, purple fumes of iodine and the smell of H2S: HI is a strong reducing agent that reduces sulfuric acid to H2S and is oxidised to I2: NaI + H2SO4 gives NaHSO4 + HI, then 8HI(s) + H2SO4 gives 4I2 + H2S + 4H2O. The increasing reducing power of the halide ions from fluoride to iodide leads to the more complex reactions.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The bromide equation is not balanced: one H2SO4 gives one SO2, so it is 2HBr + H2SO4 giving Br2 + SO2 + 2H2O. HBr and HI are gases here, (g), not solids (s).
